page: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-intel is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the High Performance family. It features 4 shared vCPUs derived from an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 12.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 260 GB NVMe SSD. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average single-core capabilities but reveal limitations under multi-core workloads. The server achieves average ratings in stress-ng single-core CPU performance with a score of 1466.08 and Geekbench single-core testing with a score of 1177.0. However, multi-core benchmarks show weaker results, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 5747.52 and Geekbench multi-core scoring 3727.0. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 421.33 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth drops to a weak 36.96 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor, registering at 17.19 GB/sec.

The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention, which explains the drop in multi-core and multi-threaded efficiency. From a qualitative cost perspective, the server offers a high-capacity 260 GB NVMe SSD and 12.0 GB of RAM on a budget-friendly shared hardware profile, making it a resource-dense option for storage-heavy but compute-light tasks. It is suitable for basic web serving, single-threaded file processing, and lightweight database operations, but is not recommended for intensive multi-threaded computing, software compilation, or large-scale data processing.

Performance benchmarks show average single-core execution, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1177.0, but reveal weak multi-core scaling, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 5747.52 and poor multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.
